Rebalancing only when a new month-end signal becomes available keeps turnover and costs moderate, while equal-weighting the top and bottom names with a 2% per-name cap and 1.0 gross limit keeps the book diversified and market-neutral. runs.hypothesis: Monthly rebalanced dollar-neutral cross-sectional strategy. At each previous month-end I rank liquid stocks with sufficient history by a composite of 12-1 momentum, 5-day reversal (long recent losers), low 60-day volatility, and price trend versus the 100-day mean. I buy the top 30 and short the bottom 30, equal weight within each side, target gross 1.0 and net 0.0; a liquidity filter requires median 20-day dollar volume above 1 million. This seeks to harvest momentum, short-term reversal and low-volatility premia while controlling turnover and single-name risk.

runs.hypothesis: Cross-sectional weekly reversal with volatility scaling: after controlling for the equal-weighted market move, stocks with unusually negative five-day residual returns tend to rebound over the next week, while unusually positive ones tend to fade. I rank eligible liquid stocks by demeaned five-day return divided by 21-day volatility, exclude the least liquid quintile and most volatile decile, and form a weekly dollar-neutral portfolio long the lowest scores and short the highest. Equal weights use up to 50 names per side, capped at 2 percent and gross 100 percent, with a weekly Friday-close cutoff to limit turnover.

A composite of 12-1 and 6-1 momentum, with a mild short-term reversal penalty and a low-volatility tilt, can form a robust dollar-neutral long-short portfolio: buy the top-ranked stocks and short the bottom-ranked stocks, equal-weighting each side with at most 2% gross per name and 100% gross exposure.

runs.hypothesis: Round-0 evidence shows that a fast short-horizon reversal sleeve dominates the composite and loses badly under open-to-open execution while generating about 0.65 daily turnover and 0.49 cumulative cost; the lagged close-based reversal is likely monetizing close-auction/bid-ask effects that are not earned from the next open onward. I therefore remove short-horizon reversal entirely and build a slower dollar-neutral book: 12-1 and 6-1 momentum (open-to-open, skipping the most recent month, smoothed over 5 sessions) provide cross-sectional continuation; a 20% low-volatility tilt adds defensiveness and is cheap to trade. I select the most liquid tradable names (price > $1, 60-day median dollar volume >= $1M, eligible flag), rank on a robust z-score composite, go equal-weight long the top 50 and short the bottom 50 (or fewer if liquidity is limited) with per-name weight capped at 2% and gross at about 0.98, reducing turnover relative to round 0.
runs.label: 去中心化 · 17

Rebalancing monthly at the prior month-end reduces turnover and avoids reacting to transient microstructure noise. A dollar-neutral, equal-weighted top/bottom basket of up to 50 liquid eligible names, capped at 2% per name and gross below 1.0, should capture momentum while limiting crash and crowding risk; names with insufficient history or missing data receive zero.

Cross-sectional equity returns contain two exploitable but distinct horizon effects: medium-term momentum over the past 12 months (skipping the most recent month to avoid short-horizon reversal contamination) and short-horizon reversal over the most recent ~2 weeks. A dollar-neutral long-short book built from a composite of standardized 12-1 momentum and 2-week reversal, long the combined top-40 and short the combined bottom-40 of the eligible, liquid universe, captures a diversified cross-sectional premium that is roughly market-neutral. Equal-weighting within each side (gross ~1.0, net 0, per-name weight capped at 2%) diversifies idiosyncratic risk, while the slow-moving momentum component limits turnover and thus 5bps transaction-cost drag; a liquidity floor and a volatility ceiling remove untradable and lottery-like names.

histories.hypothesis: Equity cross-sections exhibit several distinct, partly independent return premia that can be harvested dollar-neutrally at modest turnover: (1) short-horizon reversal, best captured by volatility-scaled, one-day-lagged 5-day and 21-day returns (the lag strips bid-ask bounce and the close-to-open gap that is not earned under open-to-open execution); (2) 12-1 momentum (12-month return skipping the most recent month) which persists over quarters and is slow-decaying, adding diversification against reversal; (3) a modest low-volatility tilt, which is slow-moving, cheap to trade and historically defensive in drawdown regimes. Because the position cap is 2% per name and gross is capped at 1.0 while net must be ~0, the natural implementation is a many-name, equal-weighted long/short book: rank the composite score cross-sectionally over liquid, tradable names, go long the top k and short the bottom k with k=40 per side (0.49/k per name so gross stays just under 1.0), and zero everything else. Volatility-scaling puts reversal, momentum and risk signals on a common information-ratio footing; momentum-missing names (short history) are treated as neutral rather than dropped. Liquidity/price filters (last price > $1, 60-day median dollar volume >= $1M) keep the book executable at 5bp costs, and pairing slow (momentum, low-vol) with fast (reversal) components keeps daily turnover moderate relative to the cost budget.

histories.hypothesis: Short-horizon cross-sectional reversal is strongest in idiosyncratic, volatility-scaled moves. I compute 5-session cumulative returns, demean them cross-sectionally by the median to remove broad-market exposure, scale by 20-day daily-return volatility, winsorize at the 1st/99th percentiles, and average the negative scaled residual over the last 3 sessions to reduce turnover. I long the highest-scoring losers and short the lowest-scoring winners among eligible names, equal-weighted per side with per-name weight min(0.02, 0.5/n_side), preserving gross <= 1 and dollar neutrality. Filters require current eligibility, price > 2, 20-day median dollar volume > 1e6, and exclude extreme recent volume surges (5-day average / prior 20-day average > 8). Sensitivity: lookback K from 3 to 10, volatility window from 10 to 30, winsorization from 0% to 5%, and signal smoothing/holding from 1 to 5 days all affect turnover and decay; the chosen midpoint favors robust turnover at 5 bps. Fallback returns all zeros if fewer than 4 valid names or fewer than 2 names per side, and uses close when adjusted_close is unavailable.

Cross-sectional continuation is best captured with volatility-scaled 126-session momentum that skips the most recent 5 sessions, combined with a short-term reversal overlay and trend confirmation. Rebalancing monthly at the prior month-end reduces turnover and avoids reacting to transient microstructure noise. A dollar-neutral, equal-weighted top/bottom basket of up to 50 liquid eligible names, capped at 2% per name and gross below 1.0, should capture momentum while limiting crash and crowding risk; names with insufficient history or missing data receive zero.
